goal_relative_interpretation.goal: Build Lean Mass with a body-fat guardrail
goal_relative_interpretation.interpretation: The pair provides emerging visual support for the Goal direction: the upper torso appears subtly fuller through the chest, shoulders, and arms while the waist and midsection remain broadly stable and lean-looking. This is consistent with the desired visual pattern, but photographs alone cannot establish new muscle tissue, quantify body-fat change, or verify the guardrail numerically.
goal_relative_interpretation.strategy_implication: The photo evidence alone supports staying the course rather than changing the plan. A future matched front-relaxed capture would help determine whether the subtly fuller upper-body presentation persists while the waist remains stable.

pi_level_interpretation: Across 62 days, the front-view comparison suggests a subtle increase in apparent upper-body fullness, led by a somewhat fuller chest and slightly rounder shoulder and arm presentation. The waist, lower abdomen, and abdominal/oblique definition remain broadly stable, with no clear visual evidence of a material increase in midsection softness. This is an emerging photo-level pattern supportive of Build Lean Mass with a body-fat guardrail, but the change is small and pose-sensitive. The photos cannot establish muscle gain, quantify body-fat change, prove guardrail compliance, or determine causation.
sample_photo_briefing_copy: Encouraging direction: the September photo presents a somewhat fuller chest, shoulders, and arms while your waist remains broadly similar and there is no clear visual increase in midsection softness. That combination is consistent with movement toward Build Lean Mass while respecting the body-fat guardrail, but the visible change is subtle—not enough for photos alone to establish muscle gain or a body-composition change. The arm-position and lighting differences make small upper-body comparisons less certain, so stay the course and use the next matched front-relaxed photo to confirm whether the fuller upper-body look persists.
